payload.friendly_name: kitty-core: shared Rust core (contract client, change stream, supervision)
payload.purpose_context: Both hosts read spec-kitty's Mission Status service, which ships as an unsigned native binary with no install location and never announces its port. Without a shared core each host would solve discovery, start-up, crash recovery and contract checking on its own, and the two would drift. This mission builds that core against the local stub so the desktop (#20) and dashboard (#21) can start on it, and reports a clear degraded state instead of crashing when the service is missing or speaks another contract. Tracked as mission-ui issue 19 under epic 16.
payload.purpose_tldr: Give Kitty Desktop and Kitty Dashboard one shared Rust core that finds, starts and watches the Mission Status service, checks it speaks the pinned contract, and relays its reads and live changes unchanged.

options: Route table from the generated routes.json over the already-pinned hyper/hyper-util client, with kitty-core's own SSE frame reader (no typed models, fewest new crates)
reqwest plus eventsource-stream for SSE, driven by the same routes.json table (more ergonomic, larger new dependency tree)
A client generated from openapi.yaml (for example progenitor) with typed models, capturing raw bytes before deserialising
Other

options: Restart with capped exponential backoff, and give up after 5 crashes inside 5 minutes: stop and report degraded service-missing (reason: crashing) until the host asks to retry
Restart forever with capped exponential backoff; the host shows reconnecting throughout
Never restart automatically: a crash stops the service and reports degraded until the host asks to retry
Other

options: kitty-core always spawns its own child process per host and project, on a port it picks, and stops it when the host stops; two hosts run two services
kitty-core spawns, but first attaches to a service another host already started for the same project, through a lock or port file kitty-core writes
kitty-core never spawns: it attaches to a service the user started, at a configured port, and only watches its health
